text: A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, his holy mountain.
Beautiful in its heights, the joy of all the earth, is Mount Zion, on the far northern slopes, the city of the great King.
God is within her citadels; he has shown himself to be her fortress.
For look: the kings assembled, they advanced together.
They looked, and they were stunned; they were dismayed, they fled in panic.

versions.text: They looked, and they were stunned; terror seized them, and they fled.
versions.explanation: 'Terror seized them' anticipates and duplicates the very next line ('Trembling took hold of them there'), blunting the rhythm of the two verses. The Hebrew נִבְהֲלוּ נֶחְפָּזוּ is a pair of passive/reflexive verbs ('they were dismayed, they hurried away in panic'), which is better rendered without introducing a second 'seized' image.

text: Trembling took hold of them there, anguish like a woman in labor.
With an east wind you shattered the ships of Tarshish.
What we had heard, we have now seen in the city of the LORD of hosts, in the city of our God: God will establish her forever. Selah.
We have pondered your steadfast love, O God, within your temple.
Like your name, O God, so is your praise, reaching to the ends of the earth; your right hand is filled with righteousness.
Let Mount Zion rejoice, let the daughters of Judah be glad because of your judgments.
Walk around Zion, circle her, count her towers.
Take note of her ramparts, pass through her citadels, so that you can tell the next generation:

This is God, our God forever and ever; he will guide us beyond death.[^1]

[^1]: The Hebrew of the final phrase is uncertain; it may also be read 'he will guide us forever' or 'he will be our guide to the end.'

versions.text: This is God, our God forever and ever; he will guide us beyond death.
versions.explanation: The closing phrase עַל־מוּת is textually and lexically disputed. Since the rendering 'beyond death' commits to one debated reading with significant theological weight, a brief footnote noting the alternatives serves the reader without disturbing the oral flow of the line.
